summary: Creates a physically based material with texture-map inputs for color, roughness, metalness, normals, height, occlusion, reflections, rim lighting, and related render features.

key_params.name: outputshader
key_params.note: Output generated GLSL shaders to DATs for adaptation

key_concepts: PBR MAT uses a physically based lighting model driven by base color, roughness, metallic, normal, height, occlusion, alpha, rim, reflection, and environment inputs.
Substance TOP sources can auto-populate PBR texture maps, while manually assigned map parameters override the automatically unpacked material textures.

Texture sampling is part of the material contract: coordinate layers, POP texture attributes, screen-space sampling, triplanar mapping, filters, and map channel sources affect the final shader result.
The Output Shader workflow creates GLSL MAT and Text DAT shader sources from the material variant that has actually rendered or compiled in the current TouchDesigner session.
Lighting, Environment Light quality, Render TOP settings, and coherent asset color-space/channel conventions are central to predictable PBR output.
common_gotchas: PBR needs coherent texture color spaces and map channel conventions; generated networks should not mix unknown asset pipelines blindly.
Normal, height, roughness, metalness, and occlusion maps need matching UV coordinates unless using an alternate coordinate mode.
Scene lights, environment maps, and Render TOP settings strongly affect the visible result.
Output Shader is useful for GLSL MAT adaptation, but the generated DATs become a shader-maintenance surface.
